clue.text: Most prudent comedian on the street

parts.note: Ernie Wise was a British comedian, half of Morecambe and Wise

explanation.surface: A comedian working the street is somehow the most sensible person around.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernie Wise was one half of Morecambe and Wise, a much-loved British TV comedy double act.
explanation.definitionFit: Being most prudent means showing the greatest good judgement, the superlative of sagacious.

clue.text: Mister ice-cream man, wife and unconventional community resident

parts.note: a hippy is someone living an alternative lifestyle, often in a commune

explanation.surface: A list of characters: the ice-cream man, his wife and a commune dweller.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Whippy is a British brand of soft-serve ice cream sold from vans, so its mascot is the 'Mister ice-cream man'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Whippy is the British soft-serve ice cream brand personified as a van-driving mascot.

clue.text: No axe-cut yet, if so ordered

definitions.text: No axe-cut yet, if so ordered

indicators.note: ordered means arranged in a new order, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: The condemned person's head stays on, provided the authorities command it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: if a reprieve is ordered, no axe has fallen yet.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprieve postponing a sentence of death means the blade has not yet fallen on the prisoner.

clue.text: Second footballer gets ahead, going round top goalie who's shirking

parts.note: a wing is a footballer who plays on the flank

indicators.note: going round means the phrase for ahead surrounds the next letter

parts.note: ahead in a race is in the lead

indicators.note: top here means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A football report: a second winger takes the lead after rounding the keeper, while someone is skiving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' puts G, the top of 'goalie', after the IN of IN THE LEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means avoiding work while pretending to be ill or busy, which is dodging duty.

clue.text: Medieval Armenian commander-in- chief on small wall on a bridge

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes
a parapet is the low protective wall along the edge of a bridge

explanation.surface: An old Armenian general perches on a bridge's low side wall.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the title of the supreme military leader in medieval Armenia, an obscure historical rank.

clue.text: Sue and Petra having clause two revised

indicators.note: revised means reworked, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A contract dispute: Sue and Petra have had the second clause amended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sue' looks like a woman's name beside Petra, but it is the verb meaning to take legal action.
explanation.definitionFit: To sue someone is to bring a legal action against them in court.

clue.text: Accepting regimes that make firms go bust

parts.note: accepting something is receiving it
regimes are systems of rule, as in the old or new order

explanation.surface: Governments that welcome regimes which drive businesses into bankruptcy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a descriptive phrase standing for the legal instruments themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: These are court orders appointing a receiver to take over an insolvent business's affairs.

clue.text: The art of making tracks?

parts.note: making tracks usually means leaving, but railway lines must be laid side by side, never meeting

explanation.surface: A question about how to make a quick getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making tracks' is slang for departing; read literally, railway tracks are made by keeping two rails equidistant.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway lines are two rails kept equidistant, so constructing them is a matter of keeping lines side by side.

clue.text: M or K? Grand!

definitions.meaning: M is the Roman numeral and K the metric prefix kilo
a grand is slang for a sum of one ... pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight over two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman M, kilo's K and the slang grand all stand for the number one followed by three zeros.

clue.text: It will examine resourcefulness and start about four on oath

indicators.note: about means going around, so the word for start wraps the Roman numeral

parts.note: to initiate something is to start it
IV is four in Roman numerals
a test was historically an oath of allegiance, as required by the Test Acts

explanation.surface: Something that judges resourcefulness, beginning with four people swearing an oath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container. The Test Acts required English office-holders to swear an oath, hence the old sense of test.
explanation.definitionFit: An exercise assessing a candidate's ability to act on their own enterprise, common in army selection.

clue.text: A clarion in octet composed as suite by Bach

indicators.note: composed means put together, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A clarion played inside an octet, written as part of a Bach suite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' looks musical but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Bach wrote a solo harpsichord piece in three movements under this title, here loosely called a suite.

clue.text: Delightful hopes scatter with this autumnal work

indicators.note: to scatter is to throw about, so the letters of the two words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Pleasant hopes are cast about with this harvest-time task.
explanation.walkthrough: The harvest hymn begins 'We plough the fields, and scatter', so the anagram signal 'scatter' echoes the hymn's next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmers turn over their land after harvest in preparation for sowing, a classic autumn job.

clue.text: Hearing not good — awful medical complaint

indicators.note: awful means badly made, so the remaining letters are jumbled
not means the letter for good is left out of the word

explanation.surface: A doctor's verdict: hearing poor, a dreadful medical problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not good' drops G from HEARING, leaving HEARIN, which 'awful' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A rupture in which an organ pushes through the muscle wall is a common surgical ailment.

clue.text: Join single person and a German

parts.note: a unit is a single individual or thing
ein is German for a

explanation.surface: An invitation for a single person and a German to get together.
explanation.definitionFit: To join in is to come together with others in an activity.

clue.text: Stable providing food for a healthy diet

definitions.meaning: steady and not liable to topple

definitions.text: providing food for a healthy diet
definitions.meaning: describes meals with the right mix of nutrients

explanation.surface: A stable that supplies the horses with nutritious fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something steady is in equilibrium; a diet with the right proportions of nutrients is described the same way.

clue.text: For starters, Trescothick offers Turner a drop of whisky

indicators.note: starters are the opening letters, so the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A cricketer offers a painter a small whisky to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: Marcus Trescothick is a former England cricketer; J M W Turner the English painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A small measure of spirits served in a glass is a dram.

clue.text: Wildly active with love and with you in Nice

indicators.note: wildly means in an unruly way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Someone energetically keen to be with a lover on the French Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective, which signals a French phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase translates as 'with you', as said by someone in a French city.

clue.text: Some sudden glitch in short university course of study

definitions.text: in short university course of study

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sudden technical fault interrupts a degree course.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviated name for the degree subject of English literature, studied at university.

clue.text: Oppressiveness of the wig abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned means unrestrained and wild, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A judge's heavy wig, finally discarded.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy burden on the mind is a load pressing down, as in the weight of responsibility.

clue.text: Craft cameramen used at machine- shop?

indicators.note: to craft is to fashion or shape, so these letters are fashioned into a new order

explanation.surface: A film crew's craft is put to use at an engineering workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: a place full of slot and arcade machines.
explanation.definitionFit: A hall packed with slot machines and video games is jokingly a shop full of machines.

clue.text: Horticultural process affected Nigerian lychees

indicators.note: affected means altered, so the letters of the two words are altered in order

explanation.surface: A gardening technique has had an effect on African-grown lychees.
explanation.definitionFit: A propagation method in which a stem is rooted while still attached to the parent plant, also called air layering.

clue.text: Lay bare at retreat you reportedly see

parts.note: a den is a private retreat

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the word you is replaced by the letter that is said the same

parts.note: the word you, said aloud, sounds like the letter U
to see someone is to date them romantically

explanation.surface: An instruction to strip away layers at a hideaway that you are told to visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link word joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip something of its covering is to expose or uncover it, a formal synonym.

clue.text: American teen hacked online forum

parts.note: US is short for United States, hence American

indicators.note: hacked means cut about, so the letters of teen are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American teenager breaks into an internet discussion board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hacked' fits the computing surface but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-established distributed internet discussion system made of newsgroups, a forerunner of web forums.
